istem:
Research question: Yapay zeka kod üretim modellerinin ürettiği koddaki hata türleri ve kalite sorunları üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2025-11-04. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions
calismalar.gerekce: This was the first systematic, CWE-based security evaluation of Copilot: across 89 scenarios about 40% of the generated programs were vulnerable, and the paper set the method later security studies used.

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced Codex, HumanEval and pass@k, which became the basis for checking whether generated code is functionally correct, and it was an early account of the model's limits and failure modes.

calismalar.baslik: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: EvalPlus/HumanEval+ showed that weak tests hide many wrong programs, lowering pass@k by up to 19-29%, and so exposed how unreliable correctness evaluation is.

calismalar.baslik: Bugs in Large Language Models Generated Code: An Empirical Study
calismalar.gerekce: It built a taxonomy of 10 bug patterns from 333 bugs in code from three LLMs and had practitioners validate it, which makes it a reference taxonomy for LLM code bugs.

calismalar.baslik: Towards Understanding the Characteristics of Code Generation Errors Made by Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: This ICSE 2025 study gave a semantic and syntactic error taxonomy for six LLMs and showed that the errors are mostly multi-line and hard to locate.

calismalar.baslik: What's Wrong with Your Code Generated by Large Language Models? An Extensive Study
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed a bug taxonomy with 3 main categories and 12 subcategories, analyzed root causes, and added a real-world benchmark and a self-critique repair method.

calismalar.baslik: Refining ChatGPT-Generated Code: Characterizing and Mitigating Code Quality Issues
calismalar.gerekce: This TOSEM study of 4,066 ChatGPT programs documented correctness and maintainability (static analysis) problems in detail and tested how far the model can fix them itself.

calismalar.baslik: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
calismalar.gerekce: This CCS 2023 user study found that people using an AI assistant wrote less secure code while being more confident it was secure.

calismalar.baslik: Security Weaknesses of Copilot Generated Code in GitHub
calismalar.gerekce: It measured CWE weaknesses in AI-generated code in real GitHub projects across 43 CWE categories.

calismalar.baslik: Exploring and Evaluating Hallucinations in LLM-Powered Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed the first taxonomy of code hallucinations (5 main categories) and the HalluCode benchmark.

calismalar.baslik: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
calismalar.gerekce: This USENIX Security 2025 paper analyzed 576,000 code samples and showed that hallucinated packages are common and create a supply-chain security risk.

calismalar.baslik: LLM Hallucinations in Practical Code Generation: Phenomena, Mechanism, and Mitigation
calismalar.gerekce: This ISSTA 2025 paper studied hallucinations in repository-level code generation, covering their types, causes and a RAG-based mitigation.

calismalar.baslik: No Need to Lift a Finger Anymore? Assessing the Quality of Code Generation by ChatGPT
calismalar.gerekce: This TSE study evaluated ChatGPT code for correctness, complexity and security across 728 problems in five languages and 18 CWEs.

calismalar.baslik: Lost at C: A User Study on the Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants
calismalar.gerekce: This USENIX Security 2023 user study measured the effect of LLM assistance on memory-safety bugs in C code.

calismalar.baslik: How Secure is Code Generated by ChatGPT?
calismalar.gerekce: It was an early, widely cited study showing that only 24% of the programs ChatGPT first produced were secure.

calismalar.baslik: Lost in Translation: A Study of Bugs Introduced by Large Language Models while Translating Code
calismalar.gerekce: This ICSE 2024 study gave a taxonomy of 15 bug categories that LLMs introduce during code translation.

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Models and Simple, Stupid Bugs
calismalar.gerekce: This MSR 2023 paper found that Codex reproduces known single-statement bugs verbatim at about twice the rate it produces the correct code.

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating the Code Quality of AI-Assisted Code Generation Tools: An Empirical Study on GitHub Copilot, Amazon CodeWhisperer, and ChatGPT
calismalar.gerekce: It compared three tools on validity, correctness, security, reliability and maintainability.

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Evaluation of GitHub Copilot's Code Suggestions
calismalar.gerekce: This early MSR 2022 study measured the correctness and complexity of Copilot suggestions on LeetCode problems.

calismalar.baslik: Is GitHub's Copilot as Bad as Humans at Introducing Vulnerabilities in Code?
calismalar.gerekce: It used real C/C++ vulnerabilities to test whether Copilot reproduces the vulnerabilities human developers introduced.

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Study of Code Smells in Transformer-based Code Generation Techniques
calismalar.gerekce: This SCAM 2022 study showed that code smells and security smells in the training data carry over into model output.

calismalar.baslik: BaxBench: Can LLMs Generate Correct and Secure Backends?
calismalar.gerekce: This ICML 2025 benchmark showed with end-to-end exploits that about half of the functionally correct backend code can be exploited.

calismalar.baslik: Purple Llama CyberSecEval: A Secure Coding Benchmark for Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It is a large-scale benchmark measuring how often LLMs suggest insecure code, and it found that more capable models tended to suggest insecure code more often.

calismalar.baslik: CoderEval: A Benchmark of Pragmatic Code Generation with Generative Pre-trained Models
calismalar.gerekce: This ICSE 2024 benchmark showed that models perform much worse on context-dependent (non-standalone) functions, and it became the data source for many bug-taxonomy studies.

calismalar.baslik: A Deep Dive Into Large Language Model Code Generation Mistakes: What and Why?
calismalar.gerekce: It classified non-syntactic LLM code mistakes (17 types in the latest version) together with their causes.

calismalar.baslik: Assessing the Quality and Security of AI-Generated Code: A Quantitative Analysis
calismalar.gerekce: Its SonarQube analysis of 4,442 Java tasks found no direct link between functional success (pass@1) and code quality or security.

calismalar.baslik: GitHub Copilot AI pair programmer: Asset or Liability?
calismalar.gerekce: This JSS study compared the bugs and quality of Copilot's solutions with those of human programmers and highlighted the risk for novice developers.

calismalar.baslik: On the Robustness of Code Generation Techniques: An Empirical Study on GitHub Copilot
calismalar.gerekce: This ICSE 2023 study showed that semantically equivalent descriptions change the code in about 46% of cases and can shift correctness by up to 28%, exposing a robustness problem.

calismalar.baslik: CWEval: Outcome-driven Evaluation on Functionality and Security of LLM Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: It evaluates functionality and security together with outcome-driven tests and shows how common code is that works but is insecure.

calismalar.baslik: Hallucination by Code Generation LLMs: Taxonomy, Benchmarks, Mitigation, and Challenges
calismalar.gerekce: This survey brings together the taxonomy, benchmarks, mitigation methods and open problems for code hallucinations.
